text:
maria: Quick check — for Private CP talking to customer VPCs are we leaning to NAT gateway egress with SNAT or site-to-site VPN (BGP) for CP agents? pros/cons? need IP preservation for webhook callbacks.

alex: If webhook callback needs preserved source IP, SNAT will break it. You can forward X-Forwarded-For but some customers won't accept that for security/audit reasons.

jo: Transit Gateway attachments let us preserve source if we peer into customer's VPC with route table entries instead of SNAT. But TGW costs and limits are a thing.

sam: Cost note: NATGW per-AZ + high throughput is $$$. For 100s of tenants NAT starts to dominate.

kevin: VPN (VGW or TGW-based) with BGP preserves IP but more ops: BGP sessions, routing churn during failover, MTU headaches across tunnels.

maria: Are there significant latency differences? webhooks are latency-sensitive (~100-200ms SLA)

alex: Latency: generally negligible for same region. VPN adds ~5-20ms jitter if via managed endpoint. NAT is local.

jo: We also care about source IP auditing per-tenant. If we SNAT to per-tenant egress IPs we can at least map back, but requires IP pool management.

sam: Another option: private endpoint for CP into customer VPC (PrivateLink-like) -> inbound connections from agents. That preserves source and reduces egress complexity, but customer must accept endpoint exposure.

kevin: For PrivateLink we need to manage acceptance lifecycle + cross-account ENIs. Ops overhead but cleaner from security POV.

maria: What about hairpin/handoff in our dedicated flow? agents inside customer VPC -> talk outbound to CP -> CP callbacks back to customer HTTPS endpoint. SNAT breaks client cert or mTLS as source identity.

alex: If mTLS is used and client certs rely on src IP, SNAT is incompatible. We could do TCP proxy that preserves TLS if we do SNI passthrough, but that's messy.

jo: Suggestion: split by capability: (1) customers requiring IP-preservation or mTLS -> VPN/peering/PrivateLink; (2) others -> NAT with per-tenant IP mapping + webhook proxy that injects X-Forwarded-For.

sam: Agree. Also run a perf/cost spike comparing NATGW vs TGW-VPN for 50 tenants for 30 days.

kevin: I'll sketch terraform for the VPN option for the spike:
```
resource "aws_vpn_connection" "cp_to_customer" {
  customer_gateway_id = var.customer_gw
  transit_gateway_id  = var.tgw
  type                = "ipsec.1"
}
```

maria: Nice. Can someone own the spike? takeaways: preserve IP for security-sensitive customers; default to NAT for cost-sensitive; test TGW+VPN vs NAT cost+latency.

infra-bot: RFC #789 updated: added 'egress-handshake-patterns' section (link: https://rfd.internal/rfc-789)

jo: I'll own spike and will post results + sample terraform by EOD next Wed.

maria: thanks — also add a checklist for customer onboarding (accept endpoints, route tables, BGP ASNs, required ports).

kevin: adding checklist items: `BGP ASN`, `allowed CIDR`, `preferred egress IP pools`, `mTLS certs`.

sam: +1 :thumbsup:
